titleStmt.title: "Walk Away": Pete Cipollone Coxes the 1997 Head of the Charles
A TEI edition of the coxswain recording from the US Rowing men's Championship Eight, 19 October 1997

editionStmt.edition: Revised edition, November 2026. Version 1.0 was the student encoding preserved in original/.

publicationStmt.publisher: Published as a GitHub Pages digital edition

availability.p: The transcript text is quoted from row2k.com for non-commercial, educational use. row2k holds the rights to the transcript and audio. They are not relicensed here. The encoding, annotations, glossary and site code are released under CC BY 4.0.

bibl.title: Pete Cipollone, Olympic gold medalist, coxing the 1997 Head Of The Charles
bibl.note: row2k is an online rowing publication covering results, photography, interviews and live reports at the national, collegiate and youth levels. The feature includes the streaming audio and the transcript. The full recording runs about 27 minutes and includes the row to the start and staging. This edition encodes an excerpt.

respStmt.resp: Recorded in the boat from the coxswain's microphone

equipment.p: Cox box / coxswain microphone recording, later digitized.

projectDesc.p: The edition presents a coxswain's live race calls as spoken text. It shows how a coxswain manages rhythm, technique, steering, and motivation over a three-mile head race, and connects the calls to the people in the boat and the places on the course.

normalization.p: Spelling is not normalized. Clipped counts (Fo', Fi') and the rhythmic exhalation "chaa" are kept as transcribed.

hyphenation.p: Drawn-out sounds (Drrr-ive, COMMI-I-I-IT) are kept as transcribed.

correction.p: Typing errors in the 1.0 annotations were corrected. Factual errors in the 1.0 notes were corrected with sources (see the notes with type="correction").

editorialDecl.p: Profanity: row2k left profanity in on purpose, as part of the record of the sport's intensity. Version 1.0 censored some words (motherf—r, A**) but not others. This edition keeps the 1.0 forms where they appear and marks every expletive with <seg type="expletive">, so that a reader can filter them in the web edition. One passage is omitted in the source itself. It is marked with <gap>.
Paralinguistic features: the stage-direction style italic comments in 1.0 (for example "(whispers)") are encoded with the TEI spoken-text elements <shift>, <incident> and <vocal>.

div.head: Warm-up: approaching the start
div.u: Eight —Cipollone is counting strokes in a focused piece. A cox may call "a focused ten for legs": for ten strokes each rower concentrates on one part of the technique, here pushing hard with the legs.
We got crews around, paddle, paddle.
Give us a little room, Penn...
Weigh enough, watch the oars on port side... ok, all eight ready, go.
Ok, how do you guys feel on warmup? Everybody's ready?

div.head: The race
div.note: After the warm-up has set the rhythm and raised the athletes' heart rates, the crews enter the course in their assigned order. In a head race, crews start one at a time and race the clock. The order in 1997 was based on earlier results, and US Rowing started first.
div.u: This is the start of the Championship 8. Ok, let's get started. US Rowing on the paddle, ready, row!
Ok, half power on this finish, good, sharp and clean. Ok guys, they're going to stall, so let's f—g walk away, relaxed, 90 percent now... three to build...
Legs! Give it! Nail this motherf—r, now! You're on!
In two, we shift two beats!
Now Madigan, go! Take that handle with you, and attack it. That's it.

incident.desc: The calls echo as the crew passes under the BU Bridge

div.u: We got flat water, A** to ANKLES, NOW!Version 1.0 flagged this as a new call. A possible reading is a cue to compress fully at the catch, but this edition has not confirmed it.
Callahan, this is your fucking seat race, show 'em. Now, go!
Legs, send, Legs, send. Legs, send. Legs, send
That's it, walk away from those fuckers!

Now listen up! One minute down, let's get focused on rhythm, and speed through. Here we go, now speed five.Probably a five-stroke focused piece on boat speed through the stroke, which fits the count of four and five that follows.
Good, driving. Stay clean, and flat. On the rudder, here we go.
That's it, port sides are cranking!
Drrr-ive.Repetition for effect and emphasis is common in coxswain calls.
Richter, you do not sit, for one fucking stroke! You drive the starboard side.
Good Giboon, good fucking rhythm. Now Philthy, here we go.
Legs, chaaa. Legs, chaaa. Legs, chaaa. Good, driving it and push. Let's walk away, driving it now, let's walk away. Madigan, good rhythm, take the handle with you, now.
35 and a half, catches stay in, stay in.

incident.desc: There is less noise from the crew's riggers

div.u: Now, here comes a headwind, sit up and drive. Legs, send. Legs, send.
Catches in all 8, let's go five strokes for catches, now go!
2, I got a line on the bridge.
Five, 35. Catches in, that's it. Catches in.
Guys, you're the mean fucking dogs, drive this thing, now.
That's it. Send. Legs, send. Legs, send.
Richter, you can see them, I want you driving us away from them.
That's it, power! You've got flat water, attack, attack
Now, 450 until the first fucking commitment, Wherley, Wherley! Now, drive it, that's it!
Do not sit! Do not sit now! Seven, six and five, go!Seats 7, 6 and 5: Richter, Henry and Wherley.
That's it, walk away. Walk — the fuck — away! Good rhythm, good rhythm!
Now listen up. Bow pair, one part drive, attaaack, now!
Work it, work the rhythm, attacking. Gotta come up one, get ready...
That's it. Back out to even spacing, now go!

Ok guys, here's the first bridge, in the wind. Get ready to commit... ready?The first bridge after the BU Bridge is the River Street Bridge. This edition infers the identification from the order of the course. The source does not state it.

incident.desc: Under the bridge, the call echoes loudly

div.u: That's it, this is one minute commitment, push. Push the boat.
Walking away, walking away from Princeton.
Drive, you're halfway through the commitment, now go!
Now, Borcherding, Borcherding, get it in, get it in, and go. Boom, in the headwind. That's it!
Catches in, 34 and a half. Who's going to assault?
That's it!The whisper emphasizes the call.
Good, coming to the end of the bridge, end of the commitment, now is where you fucking hang tough.
Good, Giboon, you're five minutes in, drive it, now go.
That's it, legs, chaaaa, legs, chaaa.

incident.desc: Cheering from around the Western Avenue Bridge

div.u: They're cheering for you, you go now! Push it!
Richter, Princeton's going to win this fucking piece, huh? What do you think of that?Richter rowed for Princeton ('97). The call taunts him with his own college crew.
Going, that's it, driving it. Guys, you must attack, now.

incident.desc: The cheering dies down. There is very little outside noise.

div.u: We're in the quiet, good time to walk away. Here we go.
The next turn will be to port, and it's the big dog. Here we go.
Driving, that's it, starboards attack it, cadence is 35, good! Going, go now.
Good, a little bit of rudder.
Starboard sides, get ready to attack, get ready to go, ready,

u.note: On a turn to port, a burst from the starboard rowers helps swing the boat with less rudder.

div.u: Here we go guys, we're going to nail this turn. That's it; going starboards...
That's it. Get ready, coming on the rudder, starboards now... Go!
Legs! Yeah, fuck yeah, USA, go! That's it, go! Yeah, driving it, fuck yeah! Push it!
They're cheering for you, they're cheering for you right now. Push it.
Now, tell me Callahan, who's tough?
Yeah, Philthy, yeah, Philthy! You tear this... unprintable, even with disclaimer (source note)
I want you to refocus. Sit up tall, and push the legs down, with the handle, Madigan, go, NOW!

div.head: The finish
div.u: Guys, listen up, 12:40 down, I think you can break the fucking record!
div.note: The crew finished first in an official time of 13:58.9 and set a new course record for the men's Championship Eight. Harvard and Princeton were second and third, and Penn was fifth. The 1997 race was the 32nd Head of the Charles, because the 1996 regatta had been cancelled by a storm. The record stood for twenty years, until California rowed 13:27 in 2017.Version 1.0 called the regatta a "32 year old race" and gave no time. Sources: HOCR course champions list (hocr.org), 1997 official results (hocr.org), and the Daily Pennsylvanian, October 1997.

div.head: Glossary of rowing terms and calls

list.label: send
list.item: Paired with "push" or "legs" to set the rhythm: push hard with the legs, then send the boat forward so it runs freely between strokes.
list.label: chaa
list.item: A sharp sound the coxswain makes on the drive to mark the rhythm and add energy. Coxswains use many calls, phrases and sounds, depending on the moment in the race and what the rowers need.
list.label: shift
list.item: A change of stroke rate. Here the crew raises the rate after the start sprint or settles it to a lower rate. "In two we shift" warns the crew that the change comes in two strokes.
list.label: stroke rate (cadence)
list.item: Strokes per minute (spm). Calls such as 36, 39 and "35 and a half" report the crew's rate.
list.label: easy all
list.item: A call to ease off or stop the current effort.
list.label: paddle
list.item: Rowing lightly, with little pressure.
list.label: weigh enough
list.item: A traditional call to stop rowing. The rowers rest their oars on the water.
list.label: half power
list.item: Rowing at about half pressure, often used to settle the boat.
list.label: build
list.item: Raising the pressure over a set number of strokes ("three to build").
list.label: stall
list.item: When a crew loses speed or momentum.
list.label: walk / walking away
list.item: Gaining on another crew, or extending a lead, seat by seat.
list.label: drive
list.item: The working phase of the stroke, from the catch to the finish, when the legs, back and arms move the boat.
list.label: catch
list.item: The moment the blade enters the water. "Catches in" asks for quick, together blade entry.
list.label: finish
list.item: The end of the drive, when the blade comes out of the water.
list.label: spacing
list.item: The run of the boat between strokes, and the ratio of drive to recovery. "Back out to even spacing" asks the crew to restore its usual rhythm after a push.
list.label: flat water
list.item: Calm water with no chop, good for long, powerful strokes.
list.label: headwind
list.item: Wind blowing against the boat's direction of travel. The standard technical response is to sit up and drive.
list.label: sit (do not sit)
list.item: Easing off while appearing to row. "Do not sit" demands full effort on every stroke.
list.label: commit / commitment
list.item: A planned, sustained push over a set distance or time, here one minute through a bridge.
list.label: seat race
list.item: A selection test in which two rowers swap boats so coaches can compare them. Calling the race Callahan's "seat race" tells him his seat is on the line.
list.label: on the rudder
list.item: The coxswain is steering, which adds drag. The crew should stay steady through it.
list.label: port
list.item: The rowers whose oars are on the boat's left side, as seen by the coxswain facing forward. A turn "to port" bends left.
list.label: starboard
list.item: The rowers whose oars are on the boat's right side, as seen by the coxswain.
list.label: bow pair
list.item: Seats 1 and 2, the two rowers nearest the bow, which is the front of the boat. Here they are Callahan and Holbrook.Version 1.0 said the bow pair sit "in the very back of the boat". The bow is the front of the boat, but it is behind the rowers, who face the stern.
list.label: rigger
list.item: The metal or carbon frame that holds the oarlock away from the hull.
